claim.pdf_says: [ CURRENCY SIGN IS  literal-7   [ WITH PICTURE  SYMBOL literal-8 ] ]  ...   (the printed page draws a TALL outer bracket that opens immediately before CURRENCY and closes immediately after the inner ']' of the WITH phrase; the trailing ellipsis sits outside that outer bracket)
claim.markdown_says: `CURRENCY SIGN IS literal-7 [ WITH PICTURE SYMBOL literal-8 ]` ...   (ISO_COBOL.md line 13920 - no outer bracket at all)
claim.why_it_matters: The lost outer bracket is the one that makes the whole CURRENCY SIGN clause OPTIONAL inside SPECIAL-NAMES. As transcribed, the clause reads as a REQUIRED member of the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, and the trailing '...' now appears to repeat only the inner WITH PICTURE SYMBOL phrase rather than the whole clause. Every sibling clause on the same page (CRT STATUS line 13918, CURSOR line 13922, DECIMAL-POINT line 13924) DOES keep its bracket, so this is an omission, not a transcription convention.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED by direct glyph inspection of the 300 dpi render (E:/Temp/specrecon/v320/spec_p320.png, sec 12.3.7.2 General format, printed page 290). I cropped and 5x-magnified both ends of the CURRENCY line. Leading glyph: an unambiguous TALL LEFT SQUARE BRACKET (vertical stroke with top and bottom serifs turning right, spanning roughly two text-line heights) sitting immediately before the underlined word CURRENCY - it is a bracket, not a brace, not a rule, and not part of the CLASS figure above it. Trailing end: '...literal-8' then a NORMAL-SIZE ']' closing the WITH PICTURE SYMBOL phrase, then a separate TALL RIGHT SQUARE BRACKET of the same height as the leading one, and only then the horizontal ellipsis. So the printed line is exactly: [ CURRENCY SIGN IS literal-7 [ WITH PICTURE SYMBOL literal-8 ] ] ...  -- two opens, two closes, balanced, ellipsis outside the outer pair. ISO_COBOL.md line 13920 reads `CURRENCY SIGN IS literal-7 [ WITH PICTURE SYMBOL literal-8 ]` ... with the entire outer bracket pair absent, and no figure note anywhere on the page restores it (the only figure notes on this page, lines 13916 and 13941-13942, cover the CLASS and switch-name diagrams). The text is therefore not merely reflowed, wrapped, or moved to an adjacent line - it is gone. The meaning change is normative and is independently corroborated by the spec's own rules: line 14194 ('If a source unit does not contain a CURRENCY SIGN clause ... the clause CURRENCY SIGN "$" PICTURE SYMBOL "$" is implied') proves the clause is OPTIONAL, i.e. the outer bracket is load-bearing; line 14167 ('No two CURRENCY SIGN clauses within a single source unit shall specify equivalent currency symbols unless they specify identical currency strings') proves the ellipsis repeats the WHOLE clause, not the inner WITH PICTURE SYMBOL phrase. The transcription as it stands would tell an implementer that SPECIAL-NAMES must always contain a CURRENCY SIGN clause and that a single clause may carry multiple WITH PICTURE SYMBOL phrases - both wrong. I attempted to refute on every available ground and could not: no reflow, no adjacent-line recovery, no convention that drops outer brackets uniformly, no misquote (both sources quoted verbatim), and the meaning demonstrably changes.
verdict.corrected_description: The finding is real and the quoted texts are accurate; two refinements to the claim's framing. (1) The claim's supporting argument -- 'every sibling clause on the same page DOES keep its bracket' -- is overstated. The LOCALE clause on the same page has the SAME defect: the PDF prints a tall outer bracket pair around it ([ LOCALE locale-name-1 IS { external-locale-name-1 | literal-4 } ] ...), and ISO_COBOL.md line 13928 renders it as `LOCALE locale-name-1 IS { external-locale-name-1 / literal-4 }` ... with the outer bracket dropped. The two clauses that lost their outer bracket (CURRENCY line 13920, LOCALE line 13928) are exactly the two rendered inside backticks, while the plain-text siblings (CRT STATUS 13918, CURSOR 13922, DECIMAL-POINT 13924) kept theirs. So this is a systematic transcription defect affecting backtick-wrapped clause lines -- which makes the finding broader and worth a paired fix, not narrower. (2) Adjacent observation, NOT part of this finding and NOT a transcription error: the PDF itself prints '[ CURSOR IS data-name-1 ] ]' with a stray unmatched second ']' (an ISO typesetting defect), and ISO_COBOL.md line 13922 reproduces it faithfully. That stray bracket is not the missing CURRENCY bracket relocated -- the CURRENCY outer bracket visibly opens and closes on its own line. Correct repair for line 13920: `[ CURRENCY SIGN IS literal-7 [ WITH PICTURE SYMBOL literal-8 ] ]` ... (outer bracket restored, ellipsis outside it), and correspondingly for line 13928: `[ LOCALE locale-name-1 IS { external-locale-name-1 | literal-4 } ]` ...
